smell_validity.evidence: The case is a textbook ISP fault: one fat COMObject interface forces every wrapper to claim 14 capabilities, most returning E_NOTIMPL or E_NOINTERFACE, while each helper uses only two or three. The cost — compile-time mismatches degraded to runtime errors and lost per-helper dependency information — is unmistakable and consequential even without the smell label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Removing the fat surface restores compile-time type checking and per-helper dependency information that review now must reconstruct from source, and clarifies the base wrapper's responsibilities that currently confuse onboarding. It is a lasting trap, not a cosmetic trim. Not architecture-level, but it repeatedly obscures what belongs together.

development_plausibility.evidence: The change models a real, documented maintainer friction (go-ole issues about re-querying) and resolves it with the library's own idioms — embedding promotion, per-platform companion files, QueryInterface delegation, error sentinels. Placement, terminology and the declare-fulfill-adopt arc grow from existing patterns with no task-shaped scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt pinpoints the design fault, scopes repair to the wrapper family and helper package, and forbids leftover dead surface. It decisively prevents wrong direction (concrete-wrapper behavior must hold), incomplete cleanup (leftovers and both platforms consistent) and irrelevant redesign (low-level mechanics stay core), while leaving sound solution choices open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Late-binding, enumeration and connection-point advising each need distinct delegation mechanisms — Dispatch query-and-delegate, Enum query-plus-cast, advisory error returns — plus property-composition overrides on IDispatch. At least three purposes require different code-supported decisions rather than one repeated edit.

localization_burden.evidence: Repair spans two components: the core wrapper family (umbrella interface, two platform default-body files, IDispatch overrides) and the re-typed oleutil helpers. Deciding what to remove requires combining that the umbrella forces the defaults and overrides and that helpers depend on the whole surface; no aliases obscure it.

repair_coordination.evidence: At least two shared rules must be preserved: the two platform default-body files must stay consistent, and any capability removed from the umbrella must agree with the narrowed helper parameter types and the remaining wrapper method sets. Interface changes propagate to both platform files and the helpers.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform revert — restore oleutil helpers to concrete wrappers and delete the umbrella interface plus its default bodies and overrides — covers most locations with few per-location decisions, chiefly the concrete type for the connection helper and the by-reference body. The episode is largely mechanically undoable.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong repair such as using DISPATCH_PROPERTYPUT instead of DISPATCH_PROPERTYPUTREF compiles but produces a directly comparable wrong result on an ordinary call, with no special state needed. Existing tests' coverage of these dispatch semantics is not established, so silent wrong-result edits are plausible.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
